title: Signature Memory-Safety Passport
description: Signature edition: each component carries a memory-safety passport — which technique proved it (borrowck, separation logic, Miri, fuzzing), the date, and the scope. Integrators see at a glance what's proved vs merely tested, and passports expire on code change. This is a Signature original method.
method: Passport binds (component, technique, scope, date, code hash); integration checks passports; changes invalidate them.
usage: Require passports for components handling untrusted input; re-issue on change.

demo.code:
print('passport: parser/ SAFE (Miri + fuzz 200h, 2026-10-21, hash c3d4)')
print('integrator: accepted; change -> passport invalidated')

title: Signature Rust ownership as proof
description: Signature edition: Rust's borrow checker is a memory-safety proof engine that runs at compile time on every build: ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes are checked, and violations are compile errors. Billions of lines of unsafe-free Rust carry machine-checked memory safety — the largest deployment of proof-carrying memory safety in history.
method: Ownership types checked by borrowck; unsafe blocks opt out explicitly and are audited; safe code is proved memory-safe by construction.
usage: Write safe Rust by default; minimize and audit unsafe; use Miri to check unsafe code.

demo.code:
print('fn get(v: &Vec<i32>, i: usize) -> Option<&i32>')
print('borrowck: lifetimes sound -> no use-after-free possible')

title: Signature Garbage collection as safety
description: Signature edition: GC is a memory-safety proof by construction: use-after-free and double-free are impossible when the collector owns deallocation. Managed runtimes (JVM, Go, .NET) trade deterministic timing for this guarantee — the oldest, most deployed memory-safety engine there is.
method: Collector traces reachability; frees only unreachable objects; the mutator can't corrupt the heap through deallocation.
usage: Prefer GC languages where pause times allow; the safety is structural, not per-program.

demo.code:
print('Go: object unreachable -> collected; no manual free exists')
print('use-after-free: IMPOSSIBLE by construction')

title: Signature Shape analysis for heap structures
description: Signature edition: Shape analysis abstracts the heap into shape graphs — 'this region is a null-terminated singly-linked list' — and proves operations preserve the shape. TVLA pioneered it; modern analyzers prove list/tree manipulations memory-safe without annotations, handling the aliasing that defeats simpler analyses.
method: Abstract heap as shape graphs with summary nodes; transfer functions update shapes; prove dereferences always hit allocated nodes.
usage: Apply to container and data-structure code; let the analyzer discover the shapes.

demo.code:
print('shape: region R is null-terminated list')
print('insert(): shape preserved, all derefs allocated -> SAFE')

title: Signature CHERI capabilities
description: Signature edition: CHERI replaces raw pointers with hardware capabilities — pointers carrying bounds, permissions, and validity that the hardware enforces on every access. Buffer overflows and control-flow hijacks trap in hardware. It's memory safety as architecture, proved down to the ISA.
method: Capabilities in registers/memory; monotonicity (can't forge or widen); hardware checks per dereference; compartmentalization built in.
usage: Target CHERI platforms for high-assurance deployments; compartmentalize with capabilities.

demo.code:
print('capability: bounds [0x1000,0x1100), perms RW')
print('access 0x1200 -> hardware trap (bounds violated)')

title: Signature Fuzzing + sanitizers pipeline
description: Signature edition: The pragmatic memory-safety engine: coverage-guided fuzzing under ASan/UBSan/MSan, running continuously. Google's OSS-Fuzz found tens of thousands of memory bugs this way. It's not a proof, but as an ongoing bug-finding operation it complements provers — find the bugs fast, prove the critical paths.
method: Fuzz harnesses per parser/entry point; run under all sanitizers; triage crashes; add regression tests; keep fuzzing continuously.
usage: Fuzz every input parser continuously; combine all three sanitizers; never close a crash without a regression test.

demo.code:
print('fuzz target parse_packet: 48h, ASan+UBSan')
print('3 heap overflows found -> fixed -> regression tests added')

title: Signature Bounds-checking instrumentation
description: Signature edition: Hardware and compiler bounds checking (Intel MPX historically, ARM MTE now, SoftBound+CETS) enforce spatial and temporal safety at runtime: every pointer carries bounds, every dereference is checked. MTE's tagged memory catches overflows in production with low overhead — enforcement as the proof's runtime twin.
method: Tag memory and pointers; check tags/bounds on access; violations trap; deploy on capable hardware for production protection.
usage: Enable MTE/CHERI where hardware allows; treat traps as security events, not just bugs.

demo.code:
print('MTE: pointer tag 0x3, memory tag 0x7 -> MISMATCH')
print('trap: buffer overflow stopped before corruption')

title: Signature AddressSanitizer dynamic checking
description: Signature edition: ASan instruments every memory access with shadow-memory checks, catching overflows, use-after-free, and double-free at runtime with ~2x slowdown. It's not a proof, but as a bug-finding engine in CI and fuzzing it's unmatched — most memory bugs are found by ASan before any prover runs.
method: Compile with -fsanitize=address; run tests and fuzzers; triage reports; fix; the shadow memory tracks validity per byte.
usage: Run ASan on all tests and fuzzing; treat reports as P0; combine with UBSan and MSan.

demo.code:
print('ASan: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x602000000013')
print('READ of size 4 at line 88 -> report with stack trace')

title: Signature Verified allocators
description: Signature edition: The allocator is the foundation: verified allocators (like the one in CompCert-adjacent work, or the verified malloc in the Ironclad project) prove that malloc/free never corrupt the heap. Proving the allocator sound means every program above it reasons about a correct heap.
method: Specify allocator invariants (free lists valid, no overlap); prove malloc/free preserve them; the proof covers the heap foundation.
usage: Use verified allocators for high-assurance systems; otherwise, fuzz and sanitize the allocator heavily.

demo.code:
print('verified malloc: free-list invariants proved')
print('all programs above reason about a correct heap')
